lines.text: This is MARSAD one's flight computer, running in simulation.
An Arduino stands in for our flight computer, wired to the same sensors.
A temperature sensor watches the battery. A light sensor spots eclipse.
A knob plays battery voltage, three lights show the mode, and a servo deploys the antenna.
Every second, the code picks a mode: safe, charging, imaging, or ground pass.
Power on. Battery full, sun in view: the green imaging light comes on.
Five seconds after separation, the servo swings the antenna out.
Every ten seconds, a ground pass. The blue downlink light takes over.
Every reading streams out as J S O N, the format our live dashboard reads.
Same logic, same data, from the bench to orbit.
